**Part (1).** m ∥ n means √3 sin x · sin x − sin x · cos x = 0, i.e. sin x (√3 sin x − cos x) = 0.

So sin x = 0 or tan x = 1/√3 (when cos x ≠ 0; if cos x = 0 then sin x = ±1 and √3 sin x ≠ 0, so no solution there).

On [0, π/2]: sin x = 0 gives x = 0; tan x = √3/3 gives x = π/6.

Note: with x = 0, n = (1, 0) and m = (0, 0). The zero vector is parallel to every vector, so x = 0 satisfies the parallel condition under the standard convention (zero vector is parallel to any vector, and the determinant condition holds). So the solutions are x = 0 or x = π/6.

Many textbook answers state only x = π/6, assuming nonzero vectors (sin x ≠ 0). Under the determinant condition given, both x = 0 and x = π/6 satisfy it. Since the problem states no nonzero requirement, the complete answer is x = 0 or x = π/6.

**Part (2).** f(x) = √3 sin x cos x + sin²x = (√3/2) sin 2x + (1 − cos 2x)/2 = sin(2x − π/6) + 1/2.

Smallest positive period: T = 2π/2 = π.

Increasing when −π/2 + 2kπ ≤ 2x − π/6 ≤ π/2 + 2kπ, i.e. −π/6 + kπ ≤ x ≤ π/3 + kπ.

Increasing intervals: [kπ − π/6, kπ + π/3], k ∈ ℤ.

Final answer: (1) x = 0 or x = π/6 (x = π/6 if m is required to be nonzero); (2) f(x) = sin(2x − π/6) + 1/2, smallest positive period π, increasing on [kπ − π/6, kπ + π/3], k ∈ ℤ.
